reviewedBy: Claude Opus 5 — every share card was advertised on the internal pages.dev origin
method: Caught by verifying the previous change on the live site rather than trusting the preview. Every og:image on this app was built from url.origin — but the router refetches from nino-chavez-photography.pages.dev, so inside the app url.origin IS the Pages origin. Read off the live album page: og:image was https://nino-chavez-photography.pages.dev/photography/albums/chicago-big-dig-2026-north-avenue-beach-1BlKk4/og.png. It resolved, so nothing looked broken — it published the internal origin to every crawler that scraped a share, and routed them around the edge. Pre-existing on albums and on the site default card; I had just reproduced it on the new photo card by copying the pattern. All three now build from SITE_URL. Verified in a preview build across a photo page, an album page and a plain page: og:image is https://ninochavez.co/photography/... in all three, no pages.dev and no localhost. The 'unfurls on whichever host served the page' rationale in the original comments was written when photography.ninochavez.co still served this app; that host now 301s, which is what made the reasoning stale rather than wrong at the time.
